question: For the remaining candidate discriminator: does a follower-side LogStore.StoreLogs failure reach the same published-versus-durable configuration divergence as the leader-side path, and what do other failure timings leave inconsistent?
rationale: This exploration tests the follower half of the narrowed discriminator on candidate 0a6d446a083a42cf91e99726f577eaea and leaves the leader-side result (confirmed direct check 3b256fe6f42b4154b75d4d2ec02e27bf, execution 452a068dbfa1488ea15bc730a0f1e7bd) untouched. Method: two in-process nodes are bootstrapped with both addresses as voters, their InmemTransports are connected to each other, both Rafts are started, one node is detected as leader, and the follower's LogStore wrapper is set to fail every StoreLogs call while the leader runs a real AddVoter. Observed (CA_EVENT follower_store_failure): the failing follower attempted 8 store writes and all 8 failed (store_log_attempts 8, store_log_failures 8), yet follower_published_phantom is false, follower_servers_after equals follower_servers_before, follower_durable_before and follower_durable_after are both 2 and follower_last_index is 2. That is a bounded negative result for this path, and it matches the source: appendEntries stores the new entries and only then calls processConfigurationLogEntry, so a StoreLogs error returns before any configuration is published and before setLastLog advances the cached last index (src-follower-gate material covers the corresponding runFollower gate; the store call order is in the appendEntries tail of the same test harness reading). Boundaries and what is NOT decided here: this run does not exercise a failure that occurs after a log truncation has already deleted a conflicting suffix, where the same appendEntries path returns before setLastLog and the cached last-log can then be higher than the store content, which is the timing this discriminator still lists; that remainder is a sourced hypothesis, not an observation. The fault is still injected at the real LogStore boundary, and the two-node cluster is in-memory. Reusing the same harness keeps the earlier leader-side events available in the same clean-copy execution, so this submission adds the follower probe without weakening the retained confirmation.
